title.narrative: Supporting development and implementation of youth policies

description.narrative: This activity is designed with a clear focus on the first strategic priority of Output 6.4 in mind, and a marginal attention to the third priority, as summarized here. The activity will support member states in Southern Africa to develop and/or review youth policies, ensuring that the processes are evidence-based, inclusive, and rights-centered, and importantly engage young people not just as beneficiaries but as active participants in the co-creation and implementation, further prioritizing building their respective capacities to do so. Related to the above, the activity will also support follow up actions, including in particular, convening of three national and one regional intergenerational dialogues on youth mental health, specifically targeting the three Southern African countries (Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe) that participated in the first UNESCO Global Outlook study on the topic, Youth Mental Health in times of Crises, culminating in the publication by the same title. In both cases, these interventions will leverage the use of institutional assets, tools, and products, including but not limited to the UNESCO Toolbox for Youth Policy and Programming, to support implementation. Finally, effort will be made, albeit in a marginal way, to contribute to the third strategic priority, which will support the establishment of a regional youth network operating under the auspices of the respective National Commissions for UNESCO in Southern Africa, to provide a platform for young people to meaningfully contribute to addressing the consequences of all manner of social and contemporary issues ranging from the rapid evolution of digital technologies and climate change, to the multidimensional crises of youth mental health, and their impact on society, in a coordinated manner.
